transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-03-18 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (Redwood CSM), Raj Patel (Cascade Head of ML), Ellen Wu (Cascade SRE), Marcus Green (Cascade Platform)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be noisy):
- Short outage cascade while autoscaling in dedicated pool caused elevated latency and dropped requests; suspect interaction between prefix KV cache eviction and large multi-request batching.
- Agreed immediate mitigations: enable request-level circuit breaker, reduce max-batch-size to 8, enforce prefix caching TTL increase for 6 hours, plan hotfix for cache eviction heuristic.
- Next: logs and traces, maintenance window, run soak test.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: okay, thanks everyone for hopping on in short notice, um this is Maya from Redwood, we wanted to go over the sequence from last night's incident and lock down a remediation plan, Priya's here for follow up and Liam will drive the technical bits.
[00:18] Raj Patel: hi all, thanks. rough night for us — about 22:30 UTC we started seeing elevated tail latency then a cascade of retries which made things worse. we had some dropped requests and users saw errors.
[00:30] Ellen Wu: yep, we saw the error rate spike, CPU on the dedicated pool jumped, and then the autoscaler created extra pods which seemed to make the kv cache miss rate higher, it felt like a feedback loop.
[00:45] Liam O'Connor: mm-hmm, that's what our initial traces show too — when nodes scale up, the in-memory prefix cache warms slowly and a lot of requests miss, leading to heavier backend work. we also observed some long-kv read latencies that shouldn't be there.
[01:05] Marcus Green: just to be clear, we were on Redwood Dedicated with the 8xA100 pool, yes?
[01:10] Maya Chen: yes, dedicated pool with burst autoscale enabled, 8 GPUs baseline, can burst to 12.
[01:18] Raj Patel: we had a bump in traffic from a batch job at 22:25 which coincided with a new model rollout earlier that hour. not sure if the model changelog matters but thought i'd mention it.
[01:35] Liam O'Connor: it's relevant — different model versions have slightly different kv cache patterns, and if the new model increases attention context or uses larger key sizes that will increase cache footprint.
[01:50] Ellen Wu: when you say kv cache pattern, what's the eviction algorithm? LRU? something custom?
[01:56] Liam O'Connor: currently it's a size-aware LRU with some heuristics for prefix reuse, but the heuristic doesn't account for cross-node warmup which is what bit us. there is also a TTL that's relatively low for prefix entries to conserve memory.
[02:20] Raj Patel: so the autoscaler made nodes, but the cache TTL meant the fresh copies weren't shared and we hit the backend too hard?
[02:25] Liam O'Connor: yeah, and because requests were batched aggressively — batch sizes up to 32 in the config — the backend work per miss was amplified.
[02:40] Maya Chen: ok, let's walk mitigation steps. first short-term: we propose temporarily lowering max-batch-size to 8 and increasing TTL for prefix cache to 6 hours for the next 24 hours while we run a soak. that should reduce the amplification.
[02:58] Ellen Wu: lowering batch size will increase request rate, could that increase per-request overhead?
[03:04] Liam O'Connor: it will increase qps but reduces head-of-line amplification; net CPU should drop because work per request is smaller. we modeled this on a similar customer case.
[03:20] Marcus Green: can we do a circuit breaker so if error rate or tail latency breaches thresholds, we throttle or route to a lighter-weight model?
[03:27] Maya Chen: yes, Redwood supports route-level fallback and circuit-breaker policies. we can push a temporary policy that routes 30% of traffic to the smaller 'latency-optimized' variant and short-circuits after X errors.
[03:40] Raj Patel: that would help. also we need the logs and traces from Redwood, we want time-aligned traces with token-level latencies around 22:25-23:05.
[03:48] Priya Rao: we'll bundle the anonymized token traces and the relevant KV-cache debug dump, we'll scrub PII, and send to your SREs.
[03:56] Ellen Wu: good. timeline?
[04:00] Priya Rao: we can get that out by end of day 2026-03-20.
[04:05] Ellen Wu: ok.
[04:10] [04:10] Speaker 1: uh, small nit — is there any indication of network flapping between nodes, or is this all local memory warmup?
[04:16] Liam O'Connor: network traces look normal; the pattern points at warmup + eviction. we did see a spike in inter-node cold misses.
[04:28] Raj Patel: we also had some internal retries in our service because we treat 500s as retriable; maybe we should not for a short window.
[04:36] Ellen Wu: yes, temporary adjust retry policy makes sense. we'll change our client side to not retry 500s for 15 minutes during the remediation.
[04:44] Maya Chen: great, so immediate items: TTL bump, lower batch, circuit-breaker/fallback policy, adjust customer retries, and send logs.
[04:55] Raj Patel: what about a hotfix in the runtime for the eviction heuristic? is that longer lead?
[05:01] Liam O'Connor: we have a candidate patch that tweaks the eviction to prefer older but high-frequency prefixes and delays eviction during node scale events. it's currently in internal QA, should be ready by 2026-03-21 for customer-stage testing.
[05:15] Marcus Green: will that require restart of the pool or rolling update?
[05:20] Liam O'Connor: rolling update across nodes will be needed, but we can do a canary subset and leave fallback policy in place so if something goes off it won't impact traffic.
[05:30] Raj Patel: fine, schedule that during low-traffic.
[05:34] Maya Chen: Can we poll for maintenance window? Ellen?
[05:37] Ellen Wu: i'm confirming 2026-03-24 02:00-04:00 UTC as a candidate slot. i'll confirm with ops and send invite.
[05:44] Maya Chen: perfect, we'll plan the rolling canary and the hotfix in that window and run a post-deploy soak for 2 hours.
[05:52] [05:52] Speaker 2: question about observability — will you add additional token-level tracing hooks for the soak?
[05:58] Liam O'Connor: yes, we can enable more verbose tracing for that window and deliver a digest plus flamegraphs for KV latency. it will increase logging volume but it's fine for a short window.
[06:10] Raj Patel: security & compliance asked for proof of controls — they want SOC2 evidence and KMS configuration details; can you provide that?
[06:18] Priya Rao: absolutely. i'll attach SOC2 Type II summary, KMS integration docs, and audit-log retention details in the ticket.
[06:25] Ellen Wu: and we need assurance that logs shared will be pseudonymized; is that standard?
[06:30] Priya Rao: yes, we'll pseudonymize and redact token payloads, only include timing and operational metadata.
[06:36] Maya Chen: noting also we may provide a scrubbed heap/profile if needed for deep debugging but only with a signed NDA — we'll escalate that if required.
[06:46] Raj Patel: ok.
[06:50] [06:50] Speaker 3: I want to call out the model rollout correlation — we should include the changelog for the model variant, tokenization differences, and any config toggles in the ticket.
[06:59] Liam O'Connor: we'll correlate model version, context length, and token size distribution in the RCA. that might explain increased cache footprint.
[07:10] Ellen Wu: about routing — could we set a temporary policy to drain new requests to a read-only fallback for non-critical endpoints?
[07:18] Maya Chen: yes, Redwood route-level policies can mark routes as 'best-effort' and route to lower-cost variants automatically. we'll prepare the YAML policy for your engineers to apply.
[07:30] Raj Patel: are there billing implications if we change pool sizes/rollouts mid-month?
[07:36] Maya Chen: for dedicated customers, we have committed baseline and burst billing; small temporary changes won't affect committed charges — we'll follow up with account.
[07:45] Priya Rao: i'll include an account note and run a quick cost impact estimate.
[07:50] [07:50] Speaker 4: any chance the KV store persistence was involved? like a slow disk IO?
[07:56] Liam O'Connor: nothing in the storage layer metrics suggests disk IO spike, it looked memory-local.
[08:05] Marcus Green: ok. can you walk through the proposed rollback steps if the hotfix regresses?
[08:11] Liam O'Connor: yes — plan is: 1) deploy hotfix to 10% canary nodes, 2) monitor KV miss/tail latencies for 15 minutes, 3) if regress then route 100% of traffic to the latency-optimized variant and roll back nodes. we also keep an emergency circuit-breaker to return 503s gracefully.
[08:32] Raj Patel: good.
[08:35] Maya Chen: timeline recap — Redwood sends RCA/logs by 2026-03-20, hotfix ready for stage by 2026-03-21, maintenance window 2026-03-24 02:00-04:00 UTC, soak/run test for 24 hours post-deploy, and follow-up sync 2026-03-26. does that align?
[08:57] Ellen Wu: yes, please put follow-up sync on 2026-03-26 15:00 UTC.
[09:05] Priya Rao: noted, i'll schedule and include links.
[09:10] [09:10] Speaker 1: minor item — can you add a short-term change to load-shedding thresholds?
[09:16] Liam O'Connor: yes, we'll propose thresholds and include in the policy YAML.
[09:22] Raj Patel: i'm a bit worried about long term — if our workload pattern includes these sudden batch spikes every 6-8 hours, we might need a different cache replication strategy.
[09:30] Maya Chen: agree. long-term we'll evaluate cross-node shared cache or a warmup prober that pre-populates new nodes during scale events. that's a product-level change, we'll prioritize with our infra team.
[09:42] Marcus Green: can you share the prober design doc once available?
[09:46] Liam O'Connor: yes, we can share a draft by end of sprint.
[09:50] [09:50] Ellen Wu: ok that covers most things. are there any blockers from Redwood side for the logs or hotfix?
[09:57] Maya Chen: no blockers — we need your confirmation on maintenance window and permission to enable verbose traces.
[10:04] Ellen Wu: will confirm by 2026-03-19.
[10:08] [10:08] Speaker 2: final quick ask — can you provide a short customer-facing note we can send to internal stakeholders summarizing impact and next steps?
[10:15] Maya Chen: yes, we'll draft a short incident summary and remediation plan and route it through Priya for approval.
[10:22] Priya Rao: i'll draft and share with Raj and Ellen before pushing externally.
[10:28] Raj Patel: thanks everyone.
[10:31] [10:31] CROSSTALK: (brief)
[10:35] Maya Chen: thanks all, we'll follow up with tickets and the RCA timeline.
[10:40] Ellen Wu: thanks.
[10:43] Marcus Green: thanks, bye.
[10:45] Meeting end.

Post-call notes (auto):
- Agreed temporary config: max-batch-size=8, prefix-cache-ttl=6h, route fallback 30% to latency-optimized variant, client retry suppression for 500s during mitigation window.
- Hotfix target: 2026-03-21 for stage validation, 2026-03-24 maintenance for canary & rollout.
- Deliverables: RCA + anonymized traces (Redwood), SOC2 + KMS docs (Redwood), maintenance invite (Cascade).

End of transcript.
